title: Of First Importance
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: The gospel was costly, necessary, foretold, real and proven. Deliver it, because it is of first importance.
exhortation: Right here we have our faith. This is the gospel of Jesus Christ. So what is the gospel?
Christ died. This was a costly gospel. It did not come cheap. Jesus gave his life and poured out his blood so that this could be true for anyone who calls on his name.

For our sins. This was a necessary gospel. There was no other way. Jesus himself asked if there was another way. Would the Father have refused that request if salvation could have come any other way than through his blood? It was the only way to pay the cost of our sin against a holy God.

In accordance with the Scriptures. This was not plan B. God wasn't scrambling for a solution after man fell. The prophets foretold it, the whole Old Testament foreshadowed it, and every moment of Jesus' life demonstrated it.
He was buried. The work was finished. It was a real death, not a metaphor. The disciples didn't hide his body somewhere. He was beaten, scourged, pierced and killed, and he was laid in a grave.

He was raised. Death, the undefeated enemy of mankind up to that point, was finally defeated and made a toothless lion. The work of Christ was sealed and proven in his resurrection. And again, in accordance with the Scriptures: there is not one action in the gospel story that God did not call ahead of time. You can read the whole story of the Bible and see the plan of God scattered throughout.

Now go back to how Paul starts: "I delivered to you as of first importance." What do we do with the gospel? We deliver it. If you could have one conversation today, with someone in your family or a coworker, make it the gospel. There is no greater or more powerful truth we can give to anyone we care about. There is nothing greater to give ourselves to than this glorious gospel of Jesus Christ.
prayer: Jesus, all the praise, glory and honor go to you for your willing sacrifice on our behalf: laying down your life to bear our sins so that we might be forgiven and justified before you, and pouring on us all the righteousness and blessing that Christ deserves. What a glorious future we have because of what you've done, restored to you in everlasting life.

May we run this race with hearts full of gratitude and strength found in the joy of your salvation, so that we finish well and hear the words, "Well done, good and faithful servant." Give us strength for today. We pray in Jesus' name. Amen.
